title: Pan de Queso (Colombian Cheese Rolls)
description:
Olivia’s Cuisine, via Sarah Gall: “Guys, you have to promise to love me forever. I’ve been wanting to post a Brazilian Cheese Bread (aka Pão de Queijo) recipe here ever since I started my blog, almost a year ago. These are OMG this is the best cheese bread I’ve ever eaten.”
Pan de Queso, also known as Pan de Yuca, or Colombian cheese rolls are delicious, pillowy, cheesy rolls that are naturally gluten-free! There also known as Pão de Queijo, South American Cheesy Bread. And, they’re a relative to the French Gougères.
ingredients: ¾ cup grated parmesan or cotija cheese
½ cup shredded Mozzarella or Manchego cheese
directions: Preheat oven to 400F degrees with a rack in the middle.
Combine the milk, water, oil and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil over medium high heat.

Add the tapioca flour to the bowl of a stand mixer and, once the milk mixture boils, pour it over the flour. Turn the mixer on and mix it well. The texture will be fondant-like, really white and sticky.
With the mixer still on, add the egg, one at a time. You will think they won't mix, since the tapioca flour mixture is so sticky, but hang in there cause they will.
Once the egg is incorporated, add the cheese, a little at a time, until fully incorporated.
The dough is supposed to be soft and sticky. However, if you're worried it's too liquidy, add some more tapioca flour. Just don't over do it or your cheese bread will be tough and not too gooey.
To shape the balls, wet your hands with cold water and, using a spoon, scoop some of the dough to shape balls that are a little smaller than golf-sized.
Place the balls on a baking sheet covered with parchment paper and bring it to the preheat oven.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until they are golden and puffed.
